assumptions.statement: The static equilibrium axioms of the dense matter equation of state can be formally relaxed to permit mass accumulation beyond the static Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff limit via rotational and thermal support without violating the causality bound.
Binary mass accretion and angular momentum transfer can be modeled as a continuous thermodynamic and mechanical perturbation that modifies the effective equilibrium conditions of the neutron star.
Companion ablation primarily affects the surface and magnetosphere, allowing the core mass-spin relation to remain governed by the relaxed effective equilibrium axioms.

formal_reasoning.final_conclusion: The relaxation of equilibrium axioms allows for masses beyond the static TOV limit, while the derived relation distinguishes millisecond massive stars.

steps.derived_statement: The static equilibrium constraint is modified by a continuous perturbation term associated with binary accretion support.
A derived mass-spin relation R(P) exists for the relaxed axioms.
The derived relation R(P) yields M > M_static_max for millisecond periods P.
The relaxation preserves the condition that the speed of sound in the dense matter remains below the speed of light.
Isolated magnetic-dipole spin-down pulsars are characterized by evolution along a distinct track, different from the R(P) curve governed by core equilibrium.
Massive neutron stars with M > 2.0 M_sun correspond to millisecond periods via the R(P) relation, distinct from the isolated pulsar population.

propositions.statement: Relaxing static equilibrium axioms of dense matter EoS with rotational/thermal support permits masses beyond static TOV without violating causality.
The relaxed axioms predict a distinct mass-spin relation distinguishing massive NSs (>2.0 Msun) with ms periods from isolated magnetic-dipole spin-down pulsars.

selected_direction.central_hypothesis: Under the assumptions of causal equation of state bounds, relaxing the static equilibrium axioms of the dense matter equation of state to incorporate the rotational support from binary mass accretion formally unifies isolated spin-down and binary evolution, predicting a distinct mass-spin relation for massive neutron stars that exceed the static TOV limit.
